data.name: Amarjyoti
data.long_meaning: Amarjyoti is a Sanskrit name derived from the words ‘Amar’ meaning immortal and ‘Jyoti’ meaning light. In Hindu mythology, the name is associated with the god Amarashiva, who represents immortality and enlightenment. The name evokes the idea of eternal light and the divine energy that illuminates our lives.

historical_references.reference: Amarjyoti was the name of the legendary king of the ancient kingdom of Kashi in northern India. He is known for his extraordinary devotion towards Lord Shiva and is believed to have ruled during the late Gupta period (5th-6th centuries CE).
historical_references.context: Legendary king of Kashi, known for his devotion towards Lord Shiva

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Amarjyoti can be found in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, where he is mentioned as the father of Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Pandava and Kaurava princes. This reference dates back to the ancient period of Indian history, around the 4th century BCE, making it one of the earliest mentions of the name Amarjyoti in historical records.
